chunks.label: Read, write, explain
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about reading, writing, explaining and learning from someone.
chunks.interference: Osowaru (be taught) and oshieru (teach) are the same lesson from opposite sides.

chunks.label: Knowing and remembering
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you don't know, can't remember, got it wrong, or understand.
chunks.interference: Shiranai (no information) vs wakaranai (not sure); omoidasu (recall) vs oboete iru (still remember).

chunks.label: Getting dressed and washed
chunks.rationale: Covers shoes off at the door, putting shoes on, showering and brushing teeth.
chunks.interference: Haku is only for feet and legs; tops use kiru, though nugu takes everything off.

chunks.label: Inviting and introducing
chunks.rationale: Lets you call people over, introduce them, invite them and turn invitations down.
chunks.interference: Yobu (call over, have round) vs sasou (ask along); neither means phoning.

chunks.label: Sleep habits
chunks.rationale: Lets you explain oversleeping, naps, early mornings and late nights.
chunks.interference: Hayaoki (getting up early) and yofukashi (staying up late) are easy to swap.

chunks.label: Chatting and going quiet
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about chatting, greeting, striking up a conversation and going silent.
chunks.interference: Hanashikakeru (speak to someone first) vs shaberu (just chatting).

chunks.label: Glad, surprised, calm
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe reactions: calming down, being pleased, shocked or having fun.
chunks.interference: Yorokobu describes someone's visible joy; for your own, say ureshii.

chunks.label: Heating and cooking
chunks.rationale: Covers reheating food, the microwave, boiling water and basic cooking.
chunks.interference: Wakasu boils the water; yuderu boils food in it.

chunks.label: Tidying up
chunks.rationale: Lets you ask someone to tidy, put things away, sort things out or put them on display.
chunks.interference: Katazukeru tidies a whole mess; shimau puts one thing in its place.

chunks.label: Getting the message across
chunks.rationale: Lets you pass on messages, report news and check you were understood.
chunks.interference: Tsutaeru (you tell) vs tsutawaru (it gets through).

chunks.label: Believe, feel, imagine
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about trusting, sensing and picturing things.
chunks.interference: Kanjiru (to sense) vs the noun kanji (a feeling, vibe) in sonna kanji.

chunks.label: Laundry and wiping
chunks.rationale: Covers wiping up, hanging out the washing and folding it.
chunks.interference: Fuku (wipe) sounds like fuku (clothes) and fuku (blow).

chunks.label: Hopes, worries, regrets
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about hoping, holding on, agonising and regretting.
chunks.interference: Nayamu (torn or troubled) vs shinpai suru (afraid something bad will happen).

chunks.label: Owning up
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about apologising, admitting, lying and being frank.
chunks.interference: Ayamaru is talking about apologising; the actual words are gomen or sumimasen.

chunks.label: Discussing plans
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk a plan through, suggest something, back it, or raise a new idea.
chunks.interference: Teian puts an idea forward; sansei backs someone else's.

chunks.label: Praise and telling off
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about being praised, warned, lectured, or someone showing off.
chunks.interference: Chuui is a short warning; sekkyou is a long lecture.

chunks.label: Respectful say, know, eat
chunks.rationale: Lets you hear and use the polite-speech words for saying, knowing and eating.
chunks.interference: Ossharu and meshiagaru raise the other person; mousu and moushiageru lower yourself, so never swap them.
